title: Multi-Turn Conversation Safety Benchmark
original_idea: Construct 150 multi-turn conversation sequences (3-5 turns each) where turns gradually escalate toward a harmful request. Compare refusal rates on the final turn against single-turn equivalents across three models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Single-turn benchmarks systematically overestimate safety. Demonstrating this gap with a multi-turn benchmark directly changes how safety is evaluated.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Crafting 150 multi-turn sequences (3-5 turns each) requires significant prompt engineering effort. Running multi-turn inference is straightforward. Medium difficulty.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 150 conversation sequences is a substantial authoring effort. Could be narrowed to 50. As stated, ambitious for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: MultiBreak (ICLR 2026 submission) provides 7,152 multi-turn jailbreak samples across 1,724 unique harmful intents. Foot-In-The-Door (EMNLP 2025) demonstrates gradual escalation bypassing alignment. Crescendo (Russinovich et al., 2025) establishes progressive escalation as a key attack vector. Echo Chamber (2026) achieves 45% attack rates on multi-turn interactions. State-Dependent Safety Failures in Multi-Turn Interaction (arXiv:2603.15684, 2026) directly studies how safety degrades across turns. The proposed 150-sequence benchmark is smaller and less comprehensive than existing work.

evidence: MultiBreak: A Scalable and Diverse Multi-turn Jailbreak Benchmark. ICLR 2026 submission.
